bull.b: A debt-free balance sheet and substantial liquidity provide financial flexibility while Streamex builds its products and distribution channels. This reduces immediate refinancing pressure and gives management more capacity to fund commercialization, although the benefit depends on controlling ongoing operating cash burn.

GLDY is showing measurable early adoption, recurring gold distributions and initial lease income, indicating that Streamex has begun commercializing its tokenized-gold model. Continued asset growth could expand fee and lease revenue if the product maintains adoption and scales beyond its current small base.

Broader custody, brokerage and retirement-account access can materially improve distribution for Streamex products without requiring the company to build every channel internally. These partnerships create a platform for institutional and retirement inflows, supporting longer-term AUM growth and fee generation.

bear.b: The very small revenue base is not yet sufficient to absorb operating costs, while the large net loss demonstrates that Streamex has not established a sustainable earnings model. Until revenue scales materially and margins improve, profitability remains highly dependent on external funding and execution.

Continued operating cash consumption reduces the resources available to develop products and withstand execution setbacks. Burn above management's target, combined with falling liquidity and working capital, increases pressure to achieve AUM growth and operating leverage before financial flexibility weakens further.

The Nasdaq deficiency introduces an ongoing listing risk that could complicate investor access, financing and market visibility if compliance is not restored. A potential reverse split or eventual delisting would add execution complexity while management is already trying to scale an unprofitable business.
